newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo seeking ministers' impeachment.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo seeking ministers' impeachment.

text.p: Argentina's former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo vowed to forge on with his campaign against corruption and told a local newspaper that he will press for the impeachment of two cabinet ministers.

"I will not vacillate in presenting all the information I have about characters like (Interior Minister Carlos) Corach, (Justice Minister Elias) Jassan, and (federal judge Guillermo) Tiscornia to the Impeachment Committee," Cavallo told Monday's edition of daily El Cronista in Switzerland, where he was attending the Davos World Economic Forum.
"There will never be any truce (in the fight) against organized crime, bad judges and the ministers that manage these bad cases," he said.

Cavallo last year accused Corach and Jassan of manipulating judges and said that Tiscornia was persecuting him and his aides. All three denied the allegations, and Corach is sueing him for the remarks.
The architect of Argentina's economic reforms which stamped out hyperinflation, Cavallo's often stormy relationship with President Carlos Menem ended when Menem dismissed him last July.
He has since relaunched himself in politics as a crusader against corruption, but in the process has drawn enough ire to have over 20 court cases filed against him.
The Impeachment Committee is part of Congress.
